warnings: CORRECTED BY MAKHAM 2026-08-24 — THIS WARNING PREVIOUSLY STATED THE OPPOSITE. This house's structural footprint is a single 8.00m x 8.00m square (grid 1-3 x A-C, 3x3 column grid, 9 footings). The first extraction believed there were TWO offset systems at two elevations: a roof-level one at 1.50m all round carrying ring beam RB1 (which is where dummies 1'/3'/A'/C' came from), and a separate floor-level one. That is wrong — there is only ONE. Makham's ruling on หน้า27: RB1 sits EXACTLY ON the main column grid, every run 8.00m, no prime anywhere on S-04. The 1.50m rectangle on S-04/S-05 is the DASHED roof-overhang outline (the four 'โล่ง' diagonals run out to its corners, which is what made it look like a beam perimeter), and per §329 an overhang/eave edge with no beam label and no columns at its corners gets no dummy grid. So NONE of 1'/3'/A'/C' is justified by the ring beam any more. All four survive anyway, on a DIFFERENT member: S-05 (หน้า28) draws the roof frame's solid outline 1.50m outside the grid on all four sides and runs a steel fascia/eave member 'เชิงชายเหล็ก (โดยรอบ)' continuously around it. So the original instinct — two offset systems at two elevations — was right; only the member was misidentified. At ±1.50 it is the ROOF FRAME and its fascia, not RB1. Three of the four are additionally carried by floor-level beams on S-03 (หน้า26), verified by scanning pixel rows/columns of the PNG and converting to metres off the main grid: 1'(-1.50) also carries beam B6 (measured -1.49); 3'(+9.50) also carries the small east bay's outer beams (measured +9.47, solid and continuous from the north strip down to row C); C'(+9.50) also carries the ramp/deck beam B5 (measured +9.47). A'(-1.50) is the one that is roof-frame-only. NOTE FOR ANYONE READING THE HISTORY: an intermediate version of this warning declared A' orphaned and unjustified. That was wrong — it was written off a scan of หน้า26 alone, before หน้า28 was opened. Retracted.

South of grid C the floor plan (S-03) prints a real beam — B5, plus the ends of B6X/BX — at C+1.50m, and that is now the ONLY justification for dummy grid C' (its earlier 'double duty with the roof ring beam' billing is void per the correction above; S-04 no longer contributes). Verified by pixel scan of หน้า26: beam faces at +9.40 and +9.55, centreline +9.47 against a nominal 9.50. Beyond C' by a further 3.50m (to A-to-south-edge = 13.00m total) is an unroofed, unframed slab-on-grade deck (element_type slab, marker 'S0') with no beam at its outer edge — per the beam-endpoint rule, no dummy grid was added there.

CLOSED BY MAKHAM 2026-08-24 — the y-axis north of grid A, previously logged here as open. There are TWO distinct lines up there, at two elevations, and the first extraction had collapsed them into one. (1) A'(-1.50) is the ROOF FRAME edge, carrying the steel fascia เชิงชายเหล็ก (S-05). Nothing lands on it at floor level. (2) A''(-1.00) is a FLOOR-level beam: the scan of หน้า26 shows faces at -1.08 and -0.94 in bay 2-3, i.e. a 200mm beam centred at -1.01, marked B5 on S-03, with a B3X dropping to the row-A column at each end and slab S3 in the 1.00m strip between. That strip is a real framed bay, not an overhang. หน้า26 had mis-recorded this beam as 'B5, A2-A3' (on row A), and the beam that genuinely sits on row A in that bay, marked B4, was missing from the file entirely — both fixed. Makham's ruling on the new line's pos_m: use -1.00, the beam CENTRELINE, not the printed 1.10. The printed 1.10 lands on the beam's north face, where the แนวหลังคา roofline coincides with it, and it runs on westward through bay 1-2 where there is no beam at all — so it stays in unassigned_dimensions as a roofline, and -1.00 keeps this file consistent with 1'/3'/C', whose printed values all land on centrelines. Inserting A'' pushed the interior B1 line from A'' to A'''.

Total-row cross-check (§4): S-03's own outer y-axis dimension bracket reads '13.00' — this LOOKS like it might be a mis-print at first glance (the naive read 'edge-to-C' would be 1.10+4.00+4.00=9.10, not 13.00), but re-tracing the bracket's actual tick marks shows it starts at grid A (not the -1.10 roofline edge) and runs to the south slab edge: 4.00(A-B)+4.00(B-C)+1.50(C-C')+3.50(C'-southedge) = 13.00 exactly. Separately, the architecture floor plan (A-04, out of op04 scope but checked for this cross-check per op01's precedence rules) prints '14.10' for the FULL north-roofline-edge-to-south-slab-edge span: 1.10+13.00=14.10, also exact. Both printed totals are correct; they simply measure from two different start points. No actual transcription error — flagged here only because the two numbers looked contradictory before re-verifying the bracket endpoints against a 2x zoom crop.

RESOLVED BY MAKHAM 2026-08-24 (was: unresolved). Two interior secondary beams — B1 (splits several rooms into a north/south pair, e.g. inside the 1-2 x B-C bathroom cluster and again inside the 2-3 x A-B bedroom-2/laundry cluster) and B2 (splits the 1-2 x B-C room into east/west halves) — still have NO printed dimension anywhere in the structural set (S-02 through S-10) locating their offset from the main grid; only their existence, mark, and rebar spec (S-09) are printed. The first extraction therefore left them span_source:'unresolved' with no dummy grid, per '§4 pos_m is always read from an actually-printed dimension line — never guessed'. On review Makham ruled all three occurrences sit at the MIDPOINT of their bay (2.00m), which creates three dummy lines: 1'' (x=2.00), A''' (y=2.00) and B' (y=6.00) — that y-line was created as A'' and renumbered to A''' later the same day when A''(-1.00) was inserted above it. This is a human ruling, NOT a printed dimension — every affected line and element carries a 'position_ruled_by_makham_2026-08-24_not_printed' flag so the distinction survives into training. Independent pixel check on หน้า26 at 4x agrees within drafting tolerance: upper B1 measures A+1.88m, lower B1 measures B+2.21m, B2 measures 1+1.95m, and the equal S2/S2 and S3/S3 slab pairs either side of each beam corroborate a midspan split; B1's own S-09 spec (2-Ø16mm extra bottom bars at midspan, length 3.20m = 0.8 x 4.00m span) is also consistent with a 4.00m span.

No soil_boring_log sheet and no dedicated plan_column sheet in this set — columns appear only as marks on the footing plan (S-02) and in the column schedule (S-07), matching op04's own note that this is the expected/common case.

dummy_grid_rule_check.before_origin_naming: 1' (x=-1.50, west of grid 1) and A' (y=-1.50, north of grid A) both fall before the first main grid line on their axis. Per §4's negative-pos_m exception they are still named after the nearest main grid (1 and A respectively, not left/above-blank), matching the spec's own worked example.
dummy_grid_rule_check.after_last_naming: 3' (x=9.50, east of grid 3) and C' (y=9.50, south of grid C) are named after the main grid to their left/above (3 and C respectively), per the standard rule.
dummy_grid_rule_check.prime_ordering: Final state after the three 2026-08-24 rounds. Grid 1 owns two dummies (-1.50, +2.00) and grid A owns THREE (-1.50, -1.00, +2.00). Per §4 the scan is by reading direction, not distance: x-axis left→right gives 1'=-1.50, 1''=+2.00; y-axis top→bottom gives A'=-1.50, A''=-1.00, A'''=+2.00. B'(y=6.00) is alone in the B-to-C gap and takes one prime. The direction rule (named after the grid to the left/above, not the nearest) is what files the x=+2.00 and y=+2.00 lines under grid 1 / grid A rather than under 2 / B. One id WAS renumbered: the interior B1 line at y=+2.00 was created as A'' earlier in the day and became A''' when A''(-1.00) was inserted above it — the references in หน้า26 were rewritten to match. After Makham's ring-beam correction หน้า27 references no primed grid at all, and nothing anywhere references A'.
dummy_grid_rule_check.beam_endpoint_rule: 1''(x=2.00), A'''(y=2.00) and B'(y=6.00) exist ONLY because printed beam marks (B1 twice, B2 once) land on them — the beam-endpoint trigger, not a slab/roofline edge — and their pos_m is a Makham ruling rather than a printed dimension chain, which is the deviation from §4 on this sheet. A''(y=-1.00) is a different case: a real printed beam mark (B5) lands on it, so the trigger is ordinary, but its pos_m is still a ruling because the only printed number nearby (1.10) measures to the beam's face rather than its centreline. A'(y=-1.50) is triggered by the steel fascia เชิงชายเหล็ก on S-05, not by an RC beam — the only line in this file justified by a roof-frame member, and the only one with no floor-level member on it at all.

non_grid_dimensions_do_not_confuse.location: S-03 floor plan (หน้า26), x-axis edge offsets (1.50m west of grid 1, 1.50m east of grid 3)
non_grid_dimensions_do_not_confuse.meaning: WITHDRAWN 2026-08-24 — this entry claimed no beam lands on these two x-offsets, and that they merely coincide in value with a real ring beam one level up. Both halves are wrong. RB1 is on the main grid and never had a 1.50m offset. And a pixel scan of หน้า26 finds real FLOOR-level beams on both offsets — B6 on the west (-1.49) and the east bay's outer run (+9.47, solid from the north strip down to row C). They are dummy grids 1' and 3'. Two members do stack on each of those lines (the floor beam, and the roof frame's fascia from S-05 at the same offset), but that makes them one grid line carrying two members at two elevations, which is normal — not two lines to keep apart. The 'แนวหลังคา' roofline label runs alongside them and is not what makes them structural. Kept here rather than removed so the retraction is visible; do not treat this row as a live do-not-confuse rule. The genuine do-not-confuse case on this sheet is the Y axis instead: 1.10 north of row A is a roofline that coincides with a beam FACE in bay 2-3 and continues west through bay 1-2 where there is no beam — see the A''(-1.00) line.
